assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which a tunable flat band produces correlated insulators, superconductivity and later topological states in a single clean material. It is a theory prediction followed by a decisive experiment, and it is a new quantum behaviour in a material, which is the kind of discovery I weigh most. The field it started is large, and it also connects to the 2D-crystal tradition that the committee has already recognised.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at the magic angle from a continuum model (2011). Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues reported the correlated insulator and the superconductivity (2018). Cao and Fatemi were key experimental co-authors and are not credited here, so the three-person configuration leaves a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: The experiments have been reproduced by many groups and the flat-band picture is well supported by ab initio and continuum calculations. Details of the superconducting mechanism remain debated. Recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation: the lead experimental student and other early experimental groups are not in the credited list.
Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Sensitivity of results to twist-angle disorder and strain, which limits reproducibility between devices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators created a new class of electronic matter that is classified by band topology, with protected edge and surface states. The quantum spin Hall effect and the 3D topological insulators are among the most influential ideas in condensed-matter physics of the past twenty years. The link between band-structure calculations, spectroscopy (ARPES) and theory is exactly the area where electronic-structure methods have been decisive.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical proposal. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental quantum spin Hall realisation (HgTe), following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Hasan led the first ARPES observation of 3D topological insulators. Mele is dropped from my proposal for the three-person limit. Shoucheng Zhang died in 2018 and is not credited, which makes any trio contestable. Fu and Kane, and Moore and Balents, are also important contributors to the 3D case.
assessment.maturity: Many independent experiments confirm these phenomena and the theory is mature and stable. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely complicated by the deceased theorist, the 2D versus 3D split, and the overlap with B028 and B041.
Whether the prize should be for theory, for the 2D experiment, or for the 3D discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature, and then the giant effect in MgO barriers, made magnetic memory and read heads practical. It is a clear and quantitative discovery of spin-dependent tunnelling, supported by first-principles theory of coherent tunnelling through MgO. The impact on devices (hard drives, MRAM) is enormous, and the physics fits within the magnetism tradition that includes the GMR prize.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995. Parkin and the Yuasa/Djayaprawira group showed the large MgO effect in 2004, with Butler and Mathon theory predicting it. Yuasa and Butler are not on the list, so the credit is not complete, although the three named people are the most defensible experimental trio.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and in commercial use for more than a decade. Quite mature, perhaps the question is whether it is distinct enough from the 2007 GMR prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the GMR prize may make the committee see this as a continuation.
MgO-barrier credit (Yuasa, Parkin, Butler, Mathon) is separated from the original 1995 discovery.
Parkin's role in the first discovery is smaller than in the MgO development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled non-perturbative framework for the Mott transition and strongly correlated metals, and combined with DFT (DFT+DMFT) it became the working tool for realistic correlated materials. It is a theoretical method with many verified predictions and close ties to spectroscopy. As someone who works on electronic structure, I regard it as highly consequential, although a method prize is a harder case for this prize.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt set up the infinite-dimension limit (1989). Georges and Kotliar (1992) mapped it to an impurity model, and Georges, Kotliar, Krauth and Rozenberg wrote the 1996 review. Müller-Hartmann also contributed in 1989. Metzner is not on the list, and Krauth and Rozenberg are also important, so the trio leaves out contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used, and benchmarked against experiment, though the approximations (local self-energy) have known limits.
uncertainties: The Nobel statutes favour discoveries over methods; this may be seen as a computational technique.
Metzner and others omitted from the credited names.
Quantitative reliability of DFT+DMFT depends on double-counting and the choice of correlated subspace.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskites turned out to be defect-tolerant semiconductors with excellent optoelectronic properties, and solar-cell efficiencies rose from a few percent to above 25 percent in about a decade. It is a notable materials discovery with clear practical value for sustainable energy, which I support, but the physical discovery at the centre (why defects are benign, the role of ionic motion, the exact origin of long carrier lifetimes) is still being worked out.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (2009). Park and Gratzel made the solid-state 9 percent cell (2012), and Snaith and Lee showed the meso-superstructured and thin-film planar cells (2012). Gratzel, Kanatzidis and others are not on the list. The three named people are a sensible but not unique grouping.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of efficiencies is solid. Stability, toxicity and the long-term device lifetime are still issues, so the recognition may be early as a technology, though the discovery is clear.
uncertainties: Stability and lead content may raise the question of whether the technology has matured enough.
Physics understanding of ion migration and hysteresis is incomplete.
Credit is dispersed over chemistry and physics communities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single NV centres in diamond established a room-temperature solid-state qubit and a versatile nanoscale sensor for magnetic fields, temperature and strain. This is a clear experimental discovery with a large downstream reach in quantum sensing and in biology. The NV centre is also a point where first-principles theory of defect electronic structure has been useful.
assessment.attribution: Gruber et al. (1997, Wrachtrup group) first detected single NV centres optically, and Jelezko and Wrachtrup showed coherent control (2004). Lukin and collaborators brought the quantum-register and sensing developments. Credit between the single-spin detection, coherent control, and later sensing and networks work is divisible, and Lukin's contribution is more on the quantum-information and sensing side.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent labs and applied broadly. The quantum-sensing applications are still growing, so timeliness is acceptable.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is the detection of single spins or the later quantum sensing applications.
Overlap with B033 on credit, particularly for Wrachtrup.
Hanson, Awschalom, and others have important claims that are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism is a proposed third class of collinear magnetic order, with compensated moments but spin-split bands arising from crystal symmetry. If it holds up, it is a conceptual advance in magnetism that was missed for decades, and it is relevant to spintronics. This is directly in the area of magnetic structure and spin-resolved band theory that I know well, which gives me both enthusiasm and caution.
assessment.attribution: The Smejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth papers (2020-2022) are the main theory source, with earlier related work by Hayami, Yanagi, Kusunose and by Yuan and colleagues, whose priority is a live question. Experimental evidence (spin-resolved ARPES in MnTe and CrSb, 2024) is by other groups.
assessment.maturity: Probably premature. The concept is only about five years old, the experimental confirmation is recent and still being scrutinised, and the technological impact is not established.
uncertainties: Priority claims by Japanese and other groups.
Experimental confirmation is limited to a few materials and still debated in some cases.
Is it a genuinely new class or a re-classification of known spin-group symmetries?

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made superconducting circuits a controllable quantum optics platform, and it underlies most present quantum processors. It is a clear, original, and technologically important framework. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in such circuits, so this is a natural follow-up, but I worry that the committee will wish to avoid a close succession.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf (2004) proposed circuit QED; Wallraff et al. (2004) demonstrated strong coupling. Schoelkopf's group developed the transmon and much of the cQED toolbox, with Koch, Houck and others. The credited list has four, and I can only choose three; I take the experimental leaders and Girvin as the leading theorist, which leaves Blais out.
assessment.maturity: The experiments are reproduced widely and the framework is stable. Recognition is mature in terms of influence but may be too close to the 2025 award.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize may weaken the case.
Allocation among four credited names and the transmon developers who are not listed.
Whether a quantum-computing prize should wait for more demonstrated capability.
